dpdp_act_2023_structure.official_title: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023)

chapters_summary.title: Preliminary (Short title, commencement, definitions, application of Act)
Obligations of Data Fiduciary (Grounds, Notice, Consent, Legitimate Uses, General Obligations, Children's Data, Significant Data Fiduciaries)
Rights and Duties of Data Principal (Access, Correction/Erasure, Grievance Redressal, Nomination, Duties)
Special Provisions (Processing of Personal Data Outside India, Exemptions)
Data Protection Board of India (Establishment, composition, officers, proceedings)
Powers, Functions and Procedure to be Followed by Board
Appeal and Alternate Dispute Resolution (TDSAT Appellate Tribunal, mediation, voluntary undertaking)
Penalties and Adjudication (Monetary penalties per The Schedule, crediting to Consolidated Fund of India)
Miscellaneous (Protection of action in good faith, power to call for information, blocking directions, rule-making power under Section 40, amendments)

penalties.breach_description: Breach in observing the obligation of Data Fiduciary to take reasonable security safeguards to prevent personal data breach under sub-section (5) of section 8
Breach in observing the obligation to give the Board or affected Data Principal notice of a personal data breach under sub-section (6) of section 8
Breach in observance of additional obligations in relation to children under section 9
Breach in observance of additional obligations of Significant Data Fiduciary under section 10
Breach in observance of the duties under section 15
Breach of any term of voluntary undertaking accepted by the Board under section 32
penalties.max_penalty_inr: Up to the extent applicable for the breach in respect of which the proceedings under section 28 were instituted

penalties.breach_description: Breach of any other provision of this Act or the rules made thereunder

dpdp_rules_2025_structure.official_title: The Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025

phased_commencement_timeline.scope: Short title and commencement, definitions, Data Protection Board establishment, salary/service conditions, digital office proceedings, and TDSAT appeal administration.

phased_commencement_timeline.phase: Phase 2 — One Year From Notification (+1 yr)
phased_commencement_timeline.scope: Registration and obligations of Consent Managers (read with Section 6(9) and First Schedule).

phased_commencement_timeline.phase: Phase 3 — Eighteen Months From Notification (+18 mo)
phased_commencement_timeline.scope: Full operational obligations of Data Fiduciaries: Notice (Rule 3), State instrumentalities (Rule 5), Reasonable Security Safeguards (Rule 6), Breach Intimation (Rule 7), Data Retention & 1-Year Log Retention (Rule 8 + Third & Seventh Schedules), Contact Information (Rule 9), Children & Person with Disability Verifiable Consent (Rules 10–11 + Fourth Schedule), Exemptions (Rule 12), Annual DPIA & Algorithmic Software Risk Assessment (Rule 13), Data Principal Rights & 90-Day Grievance SLA (Rule 14), Cross-Border Transfers (Rule 15), Research/Statistical Exemption (Rule 16), Calling for Information & Blocking (Rules 22–23).

schedules_summary.subject: Conditions of registration and obligations of Consent Manager (Part A & Part B)
Standards for processing of personal data by State and its instrumentalities under Section 7(b)
Class of Data Fiduciaries and time period for erasure of personal data where Data Principal does not approach Data Fiduciary (3-year inactivity retention rule & 48-hour advance notice)
Part A: Classes of Data Fiduciaries exempt from Section 9(1) & 9(3); Part B: Purposes exempt from Section 9(1) & 9(3) for children's data
Terms and conditions of service of Chairperson and other Members of the Data Protection Board of India
Terms and conditions of appointment and service of officers and employees of the Data Protection Board of India
Purposes and minimum one-year retention of personal data, traffic data, and processing logs; authorised government agencies calling for information

hard_statutory_invariants.grievance_redressal_citation: Section 13(2) read with Rule 14(3) of the DPDP Rules, 2025 (G.S.R. 846(E)) — Data Fiduciary shall respond to grievances within a reasonable period not exceeding 90 days.
hard_statutory_invariants.security_log_retention_citation: Rule 8(3) read with Rule 6(1)(e) and Seventh Schedule of the DPDP Rules, 2025 (G.S.R. 846(E)) — minimum 1-year retention of processing logs and personal data before erasure unless another law requires longer.
hard_statutory_invariants.dpia_and_algorithmic_risk_citation: Section 10(2)(c)(ii) read with Rule 13(1), Rule 13(2), and Rule 13(3) of the DPDP Rules, 2025 (G.S.R. 846(E)) — annual DPIA, verification that algorithmic software deployed for hosting, storage, modification, or profiling does not pose a risk to the rights of Data Principals, and submission of key findings to the Board.

statutory_provisions_catalog.act_chapter: Chapter II — Obligations of Data Fiduciary
statutory_provisions_catalog.act_section_title: Grounds for processing personal data
statutory_provisions_catalog.statutory_requirement: A person may process the personal data of a Data Principal only in accordance with the provisions of the Act and for a lawful purpose for which the Data Principal has given her consent (Section 4(1)(a)) or for certain legitimate uses (Section 4(1)(b)).
statutory_provisions_catalog.website_dpia_relevance: Every client-side cookie, localStorage token, pixel, analytics beacon, session replay script, or form capture mechanism must map to either prior affirmative consent (Section 6) or a strictly bounded legitimate use (Section 7).

statutory_provisions_catalog.act_chapter: Chapter II — Obligations of Data Fiduciary
statutory_provisions_catalog.act_section_title: Notice
statutory_provisions_catalog.rules_2025_reference: Rule 3 (Notice by Data Fiduciary to Data Principal)
statutory_provisions_catalog.statutory_requirement: Every request for consent under Section 6 shall be accompanied or preceded by an independent, clear, and plain-language notice (Rule 3(a)) containing an itemised description of personal data and the specific purpose and goods/services enabled (Rule 3(b)(i)-(ii)), plus a direct communication link and instructions to withdraw consent, exercise rights under Section 13, and make a complaint to the Board (Rule 3(c)(i)-(iii)), accessible in English or any language in the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution (Section 5(3)).
statutory_provisions_catalog.website_dpia_relevance: Inspects whether the website consent banner and privacy notice are understandable independently, itemise personal data categories, state specific purposes, offer Eighth Schedule language accessibility, and link directly to withdrawal and grievance workflows.

statutory_provisions_catalog.act_chapter: Chapter II — Obligations of Data Fiduciary
statutory_provisions_catalog.act_section_title: Consent
statutory_provisions_catalog.rules_2025_reference: Rule 3(c)(i) (Withdrawal ease) & Rule 4 (Consent Manager registration and obligations, First Schedule)
statutory_provisions_catalog.statutory_requirement: Consent shall be free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous with a clear affirmative action, signify agreement to processing limited to what is necessary for the specified purpose (Section 6(1)), and the ease of withdrawing consent shall be comparable to the ease with which consent was given (Section 6(4), Rule 3(c)(i)). Upon withdrawal, Data Fiduciary and its Data Processors shall cease processing within a reasonable time (Section 6(6)). Burden of proof of valid consent rests on the Data Fiduciary (Section 6(10)).
statutory_provisions_catalog.website_dpia_relevance: Inspects pre-consent firing of non-essential trackers, dark patterns (bundled consent, pre-ticked checkboxes, hidden reject controls), symmetry of Accept vs Reject/Withdraw UI actions, and readiness for interoperable Consent Manager signals (Rule 4).

statutory_provisions_catalog.act_chapter: Chapter II — Obligations of Data Fiduciary
statutory_provisions_catalog.act_section_title: Certain legitimate uses
statutory_provisions_catalog.statutory_requirement: Permits processing without Section 6 consent only in narrowly specified cases, including voluntary provision of personal data by the Data Principal for a specified purpose where she has not indicated lack of consent (Section 7(a)), State functions/benefits (Section 7(b)), legal obligation, medical emergency, disaster, or employment purposes (Section 7(i)).
statutory_provisions_catalog.website_dpia_relevance: Distinguishes user-initiated contact/support inquiries (Section 7(a) for the specific inquiry requested) from secondary marketing automation, CRM retargeting, or behavioural profiling, which always require separate affirmative consent under Section 6.

statutory_provisions_catalog.act_chapter: Chapter II — Obligations of Data Fiduciary
statutory_provisions_catalog.act_section_title: General obligations of Data Fiduciary & engagement of Data Processors
statutory_provisions_catalog.statutory_requirement: The Data Fiduciary is responsible for complying with the Act and Rules irrespective of any agreement to the contrary (Section 8(1)) and may engage, appoint, use or otherwise involve a Data Processor to process personal data on its behalf only under a valid contract (Section 8(2)).
statutory_provisions_catalog.website_dpia_relevance: Every third-party script, analytics vendor, CDN, tag manager, session replay tool, and AI chat widget embedded on the website acts as a Data Processor or third-party recipient requiring a valid Data Processing Agreement (DPA) with security and cessation clauses.

statutory_provisions_catalog.act_chapter: Chapter II — Obligations of Data Fiduciary
statutory_provisions_catalog.act_section_title: Completeness, accuracy and consistency of personal data
statutory_provisions_catalog.statutory_requirement: Where personal data processed by a Data Fiduciary is likely to be used to make a decision that affects the Data Principal or is disclosed to another Data Fiduciary, the Data Fiduciary shall ensure its completeness, accuracy and consistency.
statutory_provisions_catalog.website_dpia_relevance: Applies to website lead-scoring forms, automated eligibility calculators, credit/underwriting intake forms, and AI conversational agents that capture or infer attributes used in downstream decisions.

statutory_provisions_catalog.act_chapter: Chapter II — Obligations of Data Fiduciary
statutory_provisions_catalog.act_section_title: Technical and organisational measures
statutory_provisions_catalog.statutory_requirement: A Data Fiduciary shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure effective observance of the provisions of this Act and the rules made thereunder.
statutory_provisions_catalog.website_dpia_relevance: Evaluates client-side consent gating architecture, Content Security Policy (CSP), Subresource Integrity (SRI) on third-party scripts, and automated governance controls.

statutory_provisions_catalog.act_chapter: Chapter II — Obligations of Data Fiduciary
statutory_provisions_catalog.act_section_title: Reasonable security safeguards to prevent personal data breach
statutory_provisions_catalog.statutory_requirement: A Data Fiduciary shall protect personal data in its possession or under its control, including in respect of any processing undertaken by it or on its behalf by a Data Processor, by taking reasonable security safeguards to prevent personal data breach. Rule 6(1) mandates encryption/obfuscation/masking/tokenisation (Rule 6(1)(a)), access controls (Rule 6(1)(b)), visibility through logs and monitoring for unauthorized access (Rule 6(1)(c)), continuity/backups (Rule 6(1)(d)), minimum 1-year log retention (Rule 6(1)(e)), processor contract security clauses (Rule 6(1)(f)), and organisational/technical enforcement measures (Rule 6(1)(g)). Maximum penalty: INR 250 crore (The Schedule, Entry 1).
statutory_provisions_catalog.website_dpia_relevance: Inspects HTTPS/TLS enforcement, HSTS (`Strict-Transport-Security`), CSP (`Content-Security-Policy`), `X-Frame-Options`, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`, `Permissions-Policy`, cookie security flags (`Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite`), insecure form `action` targets, and third-party script integrity.

statutory_provisions_catalog.act_chapter: Chapter II — Obligations of Data Fiduciary
statutory_provisions_catalog.act_section_title: Intimation of personal data breach
statutory_provisions_catalog.statutory_requirement: In the event of a personal data breach, the Data Fiduciary shall give the Board and each affected Data Principal intimation of such breach. Under Rule 7(1), affected Data Principals must be notified without delay with a concise, clear description of the breach, consequences, mitigation measures, safety steps, and business contact details; under Rule 7(2), the Board must receive immediate initial intimation without delay and a detailed report within 72 hours (or longer permitted period). Maximum penalty: INR 200 crore (The Schedule, Entry 2).
statutory_provisions_catalog.website_dpia_relevance: Evaluates whether security incident/vulnerability reporting contacts (`security.txt` or privacy/DPO incident channel) and client-side script monitoring (e.g., CSP `report-uri`/`report-to` against Magecart/formjacking) are observable.

statutory_provisions_catalog.act_chapter: Chapter II — Obligations of Data Fiduciary
statutory_provisions_catalog.act_section_title: Erasure of personal data, retention limits, and minimum 1-year log retention
statutory_provisions_catalog.rules_2025_reference: Rule 8(1)–(3), Third Schedule, and Seventh Schedule
statutory_provisions_catalog.statutory_requirement: A Data Fiduciary shall erase personal data upon consent withdrawal or as soon as it is reasonable to assume that the specified purpose is no longer being served, whichever is earlier, and cause its Data Processor to erase it (Section 8(7)). Under Rule 8(1) and Third Schedule, covered high-volume Data Fiduciaries must erase data after 3 years of inactivity after giving at least 48 hours advance notice (Rule 8(2)). Crucially, under Rule 8(3) read with the Seventh Schedule, every Data Fiduciary shall retain personal data, associated traffic data, and logs of processing for a minimum period of one year from the date of processing before erasure.
statutory_provisions_catalog.website_dpia_relevance: Inspects cookie `Max-Age`/`Expires` lifetimes (flagging excessive multi-year tracking cookies), privacy notice disclosure of retention schedules, and alignment with the mandatory minimum 1-year processing log retention under Rule 8(3) + Seventh Schedule.

statutory_provisions_catalog.act_chapter: Chapter II — Obligations of Data Fiduciary
statutory_provisions_catalog.act_section_title: Publication of business contact information of DPO or authorised person
statutory_provisions_catalog.rules_2025_reference: Rule 9 (Contact information of person to answer questions about processing)
statutory_provisions_catalog.statutory_requirement: A Data Fiduciary shall publish the business contact information of a Data Protection Officer, if applicable, or a person who is able to answer on behalf of the Data Fiduciary the questions of the Data Principal about the processing of her personal data. Rule 9 requires prominent publication on the website or app and inclusion in every response to a Data Principal exercising rights.
statutory_provisions_catalog.website_dpia_relevance: Inspects the website privacy policy, footer, and contact pages for a prominently published DPO or Privacy Grievance Officer name/designation, email address, and business contact details.

statutory_provisions_catalog.act_chapter: Chapter II — Obligations of Data Fiduciary
statutory_provisions_catalog.act_section_title: Establishment of effective grievance redressal mechanism
statutory_provisions_catalog.statutory_requirement: A Data Fiduciary shall establish an effective mechanism to redress the grievances of Data Principals.
statutory_provisions_catalog.website_dpia_relevance: Inspects whether an accessible grievance submission channel or form is published on the website with clear SLA expectations.

statutory_provisions_catalog.act_chapter: Chapter II — Obligations of Data Fiduciary
statutory_provisions_catalog.act_section_title: Processing of personal data of children and persons with disability
statutory_provisions_catalog.rules_2025_reference: Rule 10 (Verifiable consent for child), Rule 11 (Verifiable consent for person with disability with lawful guardian), & Fourth Schedule
statutory_provisions_catalog.statutory_requirement: Before processing any personal data of a child (under 18 years, Section 2(f)) or a person with disability who has a lawful guardian, the Data Fiduciary shall obtain verifiable consent of the parent or lawful guardian (Section 9(1), Rules 10–11). A Data Fiduciary shall not undertake processing likely to cause any detrimental effect on the well-being of a child (Section 9(2)) and shall not undertake tracking or behavioural monitoring of children or targeted advertising directed at children (Section 9(3)), subject only to narrow exemptions in the Fourth Schedule (Rule 12). Maximum penalty: INR 200 crore (The Schedule, Entry 3).
statutory_provisions_catalog.website_dpia_relevance: Inspects age-gating/parental verification flows on youth-accessible or general-audience portals and verifies that behavioral monitoring, session replay, and ad-tech retargeting pixels are disabled for child sessions.

statutory_provisions_catalog.act_chapter: Chapter II — Obligations of Data Fiduciary
statutory_provisions_catalog.act_section_title: Additional obligations of Significant Data Fiduciary — DPIA & Algorithmic Software Risk Assessment
statutory_provisions_catalog.statutory_requirement: Significant Data Fiduciaries must appoint an India-based DPO (Section 10(2)(a)), appoint an independent data auditor (Section 10(2)(b)), and undertake periodic Data Protection Impact Assessments (Section 10(2)(c)(i)). Under Rule 13(1), the DPIA and audit must be undertaken once in every period of twelve months from notification as an SDF. Under Rule 13(2), a Significant Data Fiduciary shall observe due diligence to verify that algorithmic software deployed by it for hosting, display, uploading, modification, publishing, transmission, storage, updating or sharing of personal data processed by it are not likely to pose a risk to the rights of Data Principals. Under Rule 13(3), the DPO/auditor submits a report containing significant observations to the Board.
statutory_provisions_catalog.website_dpia_relevance: Core mandate of the Website DPIA Skill: inventories all client-side automations, AI chatbots, personalization engines, CDPs, session replay scripts, and ad-tech auto-advanced matching to evaluate algorithmic profiling and automated processing risks under Rule 13(2) and structured DPIA criteria under Section 10(2)(c)(ii) & Rule 13(1)–(3).

statutory_provisions_catalog.act_chapter: Chapter III — Rights and Duties of Data Principal
statutory_provisions_catalog.act_section_title: Right to access information about personal data
statutory_provisions_catalog.statutory_requirement: The Data Principal has the right to obtain a summary of personal data being processed and the processing activities, and the identities of all other Data Fiduciaries and Data Processors with whom the personal data has been shared along with a description of the personal data shared.
statutory_provisions_catalog.website_dpia_relevance: Inspects whether the website publishes a clear mechanism (and identifier requirements per Rule 14(1)) for Data Principals to request a summary of their data and third-party processor disclosures.

statutory_provisions_catalog.act_chapter: Chapter III — Rights and Duties of Data Principal
statutory_provisions_catalog.act_section_title: Right to correction and erasure of personal data
statutory_provisions_catalog.statutory_requirement: The Data Principal has the right to correction, completion, updating, and erasure of her personal data for the processing of which she has previously given consent.
statutory_provisions_catalog.website_dpia_relevance: Inspects whether the website provides self-service or structured request channels for correction, updating, and erasure.

statutory_provisions_catalog.act_chapter: Chapter III — Rights and Duties of Data Principal
statutory_provisions_catalog.act_section_title: Right of grievance redressal (90-Day Statutory Maximum SLA)
statutory_provisions_catalog.rules_2025_reference: Rule 14(3) (Grievance redressal period not exceeding 90 days)
statutory_provisions_catalog.statutory_requirement: A Data Principal shall have the right to have readily available means of grievance redressal provided by a Data Fiduciary or Consent Manager (Section 13(1)). Under Section 13(2) read with Rule 14(3), the Data Fiduciary or Consent Manager shall respond to any grievances within a period not exceeding 90 days (and publish its timeline and technical/organisational measures for effective observance). Exhaustion of this grievance opportunity is a prerequisite before approaching the Board (Section 13(3)).
statutory_provisions_catalog.website_dpia_relevance: Inspects whether the website states a grievance resolution SLA aligned with the statutory maximum of 90 days under Rule 14(3) and provides a functional grievance submission path.

statutory_provisions_catalog.act_chapter: Chapter III — Rights and Duties of Data Principal
statutory_provisions_catalog.act_section_title: Right to nominate
statutory_provisions_catalog.statutory_requirement: A Data Principal shall have the right to nominate any other individual who shall, in the event of death or incapacity of the Data Principal, exercise the rights of the Data Principal in accordance with the Act and Rule 14(4).
statutory_provisions_catalog.website_dpia_relevance: Inspects whether the privacy notice and rights portal reference the right to nominate under Section 14 and Rule 14(4).

statutory_provisions_catalog.act_chapter: Chapter IV — Special Provisions
statutory_provisions_catalog.act_section_title: Processing of personal data outside India (Cross-Border Transfers)
statutory_provisions_catalog.rules_2025_reference: Rule 15 (Transfer of personal data outside India)
statutory_provisions_catalog.statutory_requirement: The Central Government may by notification restrict the transfer of personal data by a Data Fiduciary for processing to such country or territory outside India as may be notified (Section 16(1)). Under Rule 15, any transfer of personal data outside India by a Data Fiduciary is subject to meeting such requirements as the Central Government may by general or special order specify in respect of making personal data available to any foreign State or its agency/authority.
statutory_provisions_catalog.website_dpia_relevance: Maps every third-party domain, CDN, analytics endpoint, CRM webhook, AI API, and ad-tech collector loaded by the website to its primary jurisdiction and recommends cross-border transfer governance and processor clauses.

statutory_provisions_catalog.act_chapter: Chapter IV — Special Provisions
statutory_provisions_catalog.act_section_title: Exemptions
statutory_provisions_catalog.rules_2025_reference: Rule 12 & Rule 16 (Exemption for research, archiving or statistical purposes)
statutory_provisions_catalog.statutory_requirement: Sets out statutory exemptions (e.g., enforcement of legal rights, judicial functions, prevention/investigation of offences, approved mergers/restructuring, and research/archiving/statistical processing meeting Rule 16 standards where data is not used to make any decision specific to a Data Principal).
statutory_provisions_catalog.website_dpia_relevance: Clarifies that commercial website analytics, session replay, and marketing attribution personalize or profile specific users/devices and therefore cannot claim the Section 17(2)(b) / Rule 16 statistical exemption.

reputation_safety_and_advisory_framing_p.policy_objective: Every output produced by the Website DPIA Audit Skill must read as a constructive, board-ready, peer-to-peer legal-technical readiness assessment. It must never accuse, defame, disparage, or make speculative claims about backend or internal systems that cannot be observed from passive client-side inspection.

approved_readiness_tiers.meaning: Publicly observable client-side signals align with the applicable DPDP Act, 2023 and DPDP Rules, 2025 (G.S.R. 846(E)) control objective.
approved_readiness_tiers.approved_template_pattern: Observed [technical signal] on [target_url], demonstrating alignment with [Statutory Citation]. To maintain continuous readiness ahead of the 13 May 2027 operational milestone, periodic regression verification is recommended.

approved_readiness_tiers.meaning: Foundational controls are present, and targeted configuration refinements are recommended to strengthen demonstrable statutory readiness.
approved_readiness_tiers.approved_template_pattern: Observed [technical signal]. To strengthen demonstrable readiness under [Statutory Citation], consider enhancing [specific control] by implementing [recommended engineering action].

approved_readiness_tiers.meaning: An observable client-side signal (such as pre-consent tracker firing, missing notice element, or unmasked session replay) warrants prioritized engineering and DPO review ahead of full operational enforcement.
approved_readiness_tiers.approved_template_pattern: During read-only client-side inspection of [target_url], [observed technical signal] was detected prior to affirmative consent interaction. To align with [Statutory Citation] ahead of the 13 May 2027 operational enforcement date, engineering teams are advised to [recommended engineering fix].

reputation_safety_and_advisory_framing_p.mandatory_scope_qualifier: This report is a confidential, read-only technical DPIA readiness assessment based solely on publicly observable client-side website signals at the timestamp of inspection. It does not constitute a legal opinion or statutory certification, and makes no representation regarding backend/internal organisational controls.

forbidden_statutory_myth_patterns.description: Claiming that the DPDP Act/Rules grievance redressal SLA is 30 days or 7 days (e.g., '30-day grievance', '7-day grievance', 'within 30 days under Rule 14'). Ground truth is strictly not exceeding 90 days under Section 13(2) read with Rule 14(3).
Citing anything other than 9 Chapters, 44 Sections, and 1 Schedule for the DPDP Act, 2023.
Citing anything other than 23 Rules and 7 Schedules notified on 13 November 2025 under G.S.R. 846(E) for the DPDP Rules, 2025.
Claiming security/processing log retention is less than 1 year (e.g., 30, 90, or 180 days minimum). Ground truth is minimum 1 year under Rule 8(3) read with the Seventh Schedule.
